verse: Though, in the sight of people, they suffered torments, their hope is full of immortality. Having been disciplined a little, they will receive great good, because God tested them and found them worthy of himself. (Wis 3:4-5)
We also boast in our afflictions, knowing that suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, and hope will not disappoint us. (Rom 5:3-5)
I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which will be revealed in us. (Rom 8:18)
If you suffer as a Christian, don't be ashamed of it, but glorify God that you bear that name. (1 Pet 4:16)
We do not lose heart. Even though our outer self is wasting away, our inner nature is being renewed day by day. (2 Cor 4:16)

This momentary light affliction we suffer is preparing us for a tremendous and eternal glory, far beyond all measure. Because we look not at the things which are seen, but on things which are not seen. For the things which are seen, are temporal; but the things which are not seen, are eternal. (2 Cor 4:17-18)
I now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and in my flesh I am filling up what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions for the sake of his body, which is the church. (Col 1:24)
My friends, consider it all joy when you face trials of any kind, for you know that the testing of your faith produces endurance. (Jas 1:2-3)

We are afflicted in every way but not distressed; perplexed, but not in despair; persecuted but not forsaken; cast down but not destroyed; always carrying in the body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made manifest in our bodies. (2 Cor 4:8-10)
I am content with weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and distresses for Christ's sake. For when I am weak, then I am strong. (2 Cor 12:10)
The God of all grace, who has called us to his eternal glory in Christ Jesus, will himself perfect, confirm, strengthen, and establish us, after a brief time of suffering. (1 Pet 5:10)

In this you greatly rejoice, even though it may now be necessary for you to be grieved for a while because of the many kinds of trials you suffer. Their purpose is to prove that your faith is genuine. Even gold, which can be destroyed, is tested by fire; and so your faith, which is much more precious than gold, must also be tested, so that it may endure. Then you will receive praise and glory and honor on the Day when Jesus Christ is revealed. (1 Pet 1:6-7)

For it is thankworthy, if being mindful of God, you endure grief while suffering unjustly. What credit is it if you endure when you are being punished for doing wrong? But if you endure when you do right and suffer for it, this is acceptable with God. (1 Pet 2:19-20)
To this you have been called, for Christ himself suffered for us and left you an example, so that you should follow in his steps. (1 Pet 2:21)

Take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord as examples of patient endurance under suffering. We call them blessed because they endured. You have heard of Job's endurance, and you have seen the purpose of the Lord. For the Lord is full of mercy and compassion. (Jas 5:10-11)
In the world you will have tribulation. But be courageous; I have conquered the world! (Jn 16:33)
He who delivered us from so great a peril will continue to deliver us; on him we have put our hope that he will deliver us again. (2 Cor 1:10)

No trial has taken hold of you that is not common to everyone. God is faithful and he will not let you be tried beyond your strength, but with the testing he will also provide a way to escape so that you may be able to bear it. (1 Cor 10:13)
This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him, and was saved from every trouble. (Ps 34:6)
Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the Lord delivers them from them all. (Ps 34:19)
I will lift up my eyes to the hills—from where will my help come? My help comes from the Lord, who made heaven and earth. (Ps 121:1-2)
In the day of trouble, he will hide me in his shelter; he will conceal me under the cover of his tent and set me high on a rock. (Ps 27:5)
Call upon me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me. (Ps 50:15)
The needy shall not always be forgotten, and the hope of the afflicted shall not perish forever. (Ps 9:18)
You have been given the privilege not only of believing in Christ, but also to suffer for his sake. (Phil 1:29)
For in hope we were saved; but hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for what is seen? But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience. (Rom 8:24-25)

Blessed are those who suffer persecution for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are you when they revile you and persecute you and speak all that is evil against you untruly on my account: Be glad and rejoice, for your reward is very great in heaven. (Matt 5:10-12)
What credit is there if you endure when you are beaten for doing wrong? But if you endure suffering when you do good, this is acceptable with God. (1 Pet 2:20)
For it is better to suffer for doing good, if it is the will of God, than to suffer for doing evil. (1 Pet 3:17)
For you observe hardship and sorrow, so that you may take it into your hands. The poor one commits himself to you. You are the helper to the orphan. (Ps 10:14)
Though the Lord may give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your teacher will no longer hide himself, but your eyes shall see your teacher. (Is 30:20)
“The Lord is my portion,” says my soul, “therefore I will hope in him.” (Lam 3:24)
It is good to wait quietly for the salvation of the Lord. (Lam 3:26)
It is good for a man to bear the yoke in his youth, to sit alone in silence when the Lord has laid it upon him, to put his mouth to the dust, for there may still be hope. (Lam 3:27-29)
You have pleaded my cause, O Lord, you have redeemed my life. You have seen the wrong against me, O Lord; judge my cause. (Lam 3:58-59)
We who live are ever handed over unto death for the sake of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be manifested in our mortal flesh. (2 Cor 4:11)
It was fitting for him, because of whom and through whom all things exist, who had led many children into glory, should make the pioneer of their salvation perfect through sufferings. (Heb 2:10)
Blessed is the Lord, my rock, who trains my hands for the battle and my fingers for the war. My rock and my fortress, my stronghold and my deliverer, my protector in him I have hoped. (Ps 144:1-2)

Dearly beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery trial that is occurring among you to test you, as though some strange thing were happening to you. Instead rejoice in as much as you are partakers in Christ’s sufferings, so that when his glory is revealed, you may also be glad with exceeding joy. (1 Pet 4:12-13)

They strengthened the souls of the disciples and encouraged them that they should remain always in the faith and by telling them, “it is necessary for us to enter into the kingdom of God through many tribulations.” (Acts 14:22)

Being strengthened with all the strength, in accord with the power of his glory, may you be prepared to endure everything with all patience, with joy, giving thanks to God the Father, who has qualified us to have a share in the inheritance of the saints in the light. (Col 1:11-12)

Remember the entire journey along which the Lord your God led you, for forty years through the desert, in order to humble you, and to test you to make known the things that were in your heart, whether or not you would keep his commandments. (Deut 8:2)
I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother; my soul is like the weaned child within me. O Israel, hope in the Lord now and forever. (Ps 131:2-3)
Our ancestors trusted in you; they trusted, and you delivered them. To you they cried and were saved; they trusted in you and were not put to shame. (Ps 22:4-5)
But for you, O Lord, do I wait; it is you, O Lord my God, who will answer. (Ps 38:15)

He brought me up from the desolate pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and establishing my steps. He has put a new song in my mouth, a hymn of praise to our God. Many will see it and fear and shall trust in the Lord. (Ps 40:2-3)
Be still and know that I am God! I am exalted among the nations; I will be exalted in the earth. The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. (Ps 46:10-11)

The Lord sets free the prisoners; the Lord opens the eyes of the blind. The Lord lifts up those who are bowed down; the Lord loves the righteous. The Lord preserves the strangers; he helps the orphan and the widow, but the way of the wicked he turns upside down. (Ps 146:7-9)
As for me, I would seek God, and to God I would commit my cause. He does great deeds and unsearchable, marvelous things without number. (Job 5:8-9)

Happy is the one whom God corrects; therefore, do not despise the chastening of the Almighty. For he wounds, but he also binds up; he strikes, but his hands also heal. He will deliver you in six troubles; in seven no evil shall touch you. (Job 5:17-19)
